Integrated Energy Policy
*301. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Planning Commission
submitted in August, 2006 an 'Integrated
Energy Policy' commensurate with
requirement of energy infrastructure needed
to accomplish annual Gross Domestic
Product (GDP) growth rate of eight per
cent upto the year 2031-32;
(b) if so, the current status of the policy
in terms of its acceptance by Government
and implementation;
(c) the sources envisioned for harnessing
in the said policy by the Planning
Commission for energy security; and
(d) the steps contemplated by
Government in respect thereto?
Link between Commonwealth Games
Village and Jawaharlal Nehru
Stadium
*302. SHRI MANOHAR JOSHI: Will
the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether any time-frame has been
determined for the proposed link between
the Commonwealth Village site and
Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium passing near
Humayun's Tomb for the Commonwealth
Games to complete the project in time;
(b) whether any stand off between
Government and Delhi Urban Arts
Commission (DUAC) over several projects
for Commonwealth Games has not been
resolved so far, thus causing inordinate
delay in the completion of the project;
and
(c) the remedial measures being taken
by Government to resolve the deadlock?

97
Use of genetically modified paddy
†*303. SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Central
Approval Committee has given the
permission to use genetically modified
paddy in the country;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
basmati rice producing areas in Uttar
Pradesh, where the use of genetically
modified paddy has been allowed would
be destroyed by the infection caused by
the said paddy;
(c) if so, whether Government would
take any effective steps to prevent the same
keeping in view the damage by genetically
modified paddy; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Protection of endangered animals
*304. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the population of the
endangered animals, including lions, tigers
and elephants, is dwindling in the reserve
forests each passing year;
(b) if so, the details for the last three
years; and
(c) the action proposed to be taken to
protect these animals?
Road linkage for Najafgarh via
Shyam Vihar
*305. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH:
SHRI HARISH RAW A T:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of objections
received by Government against
Notification No. F.9(88)/2004/L&B/LA/
176 dated 7.4.2006 issued on behalf of
Lt. Governor, Delhi by Land and Building
Department, DDA for construction of a
road linkage for Najafgarh area via Shyam
Vihar;
(b) the number of dwelling units likely
to be uprooted due to the implementation
of this project;
(c) the action proposed to be taken to
stop the construction of this road to prevent
large-scale uprooting of dwelling units; and
(d) the reasons for not constructing an
elevated road?
Utilization of BRGF
*306. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of PANCHAYA TI
RAJ be pleased to state:
(a) whether 250 districts of the country
have been shortlisted for the Backward
Regions Grant Fund (BRGF) programme
for receiving funds to reduce regional
imbalances and eradicate poverty and
backwardness and against allocation for
2007-08 of around Rs. 4,670 crore, only
Rs. 700 crore were disbursed;
(b) if so, the main reasons for not
utilizing the funds;
(c) whether Government has changed
the guidelines so that the funds are utilized
fully and in time; and
(d) the latest position of utilizing the
funds during the remaining period of the
financial year?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

98
Regional Passport Office in
Mangalore
*307. DR. VIJAY MALLY A: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government proposes to
open a Regional Passport Office in
Mangalore in Karnataka;
(b) the total number of applications for
issuance of passport received from South
Canara region in the previous three years;
(c) the total number of applications for
issuance of passport pertaining to South
Canara region that are pending; and
(d) the time frame fixed to establish a
Regional Passport Office in Mangalore?
Global warming
*308. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India is
preparing to put before UN's convention,
its strategies on climate change;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the further steps which are being
taken to control global warming?
Seven amenities and services to the
urban poor
*309. SHRI V . HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of HOUSING
AND URBAN POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
ensure that every urban resident in the
country has assured access to the "seven
amenities and services to the urban poor";
(b) the seven amenities referred to
above;
(c) the priority of each of the seven
amenities in descending order;
(d) whether any study on the existence
or absence of the seven amenities has been
done, State-wise;
(e) if not, in what manner Government
would be able to provide and evolve
decisions to meet the demands and needs;
and
(f) the steps proposed to carefully
study all urban habitats on the status of
the seven amenities?
Extinction of lions and tigers
†*310. SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that lions and
tigers are going to be included in the list of
animals nearing extinction;
(b) if so, whether Government has
formulated any effective scheme for their
growth and steps have been taken for the
protection of environment; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Prices of coal
†*311. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Coal
India Limited shall undertake yearly review
with a view to increasing prices of coal for
selling the same to the power companies;
(b) if so, the reasons for increasing the
prices of coal;
(c) whether increase in the prices of coal
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

99
shall result in costly electricity and that
the cost of products manufactured by using
electricity shall also go up as a result thereof;
and
(d) if so, the steps being taken by
Government to ensure that prices of coal
do not go up?
Opposition to revival of nuclear power
*312. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
scientists in the US and European Parliament
had opposed the revival of nuclear power;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government is also aware
that the war industries and the Nuclear
Suppliers Group countries are anxious to
dump their hardware in India; and
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Rapid rise in global warming
*313. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has come to
know about rapid rise in global warming
during the period 2005-06 and 2006-07;
(b) how far it is expected to go up during
the period 2007-08;
(c) how it has adversely affected the
fertility of the agricultural land, water
resources and breathing of human beings
and animals; and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government for the protection of human
beings and other living creatures?
Satellite based system for fishermen
*314. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to install
Satellite based system to help fishermen in
distress in the ocean;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the time-frame within which it would
be installed on the Orissa coastline; and
(d) the total number of boats that would
be equipped with this system in a phased
manner in Orissa?
Rising number of vehicles
*315. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether he is fully aware of the
unprecedented increase of vehicles in urban
areas leading to major traffic and parking
problems and at this rate, very soon, an
unmanageable stage may come for want of
necessary infrastructural facilities;
(b) if so, the policy initiatives envisaged
as long and short term measures; and
(c) whether in this context there would
be a move to restrict the purchase and
regulate use of vehicles on certain routes
and during certain hours as in foreign
countries, besides all out efforts to develop
infrastructural facilities like new roads,
broadening existing roads, construction of
fly-overs, diversions, by-pass roads, etc.?

100
All India Sarpanch Conference
*316. SHRI SHARAD Y ADA V: Will
the Minister of PANCHAY ATI RAJ be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of panchayat people
being invited in the All India Sarpanch
Conference;
(b) the arrangements being made for
their travel and stay in Delhi and expenses
thereon; and
(c) whether it is necessary to make such
a huge ‘function’ for Gram Panchayats,
when it is a State subject?
Agreement with Gulf countries
*317. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of OVERSEAS INDIAN
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has decided to sign agreements with Gulf
countries in order to protect Indian workers
there; and
(b) the salient features of the agreements
and by when these are expected to be
implemented?
Inclusion of Shimla-Chirgaon and
Rampur-Rohru roads into the
category of National Highway
*318. SHRI BASHISTHA NARAIN
SINGH: Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has received a
representation forwarded by Prime
Minister's Office in the month of August,
2007 regarding inclusion of Shimla-Chirgaon
and Rampur-Rohru roads into National
Highway;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government would include
these roads during the Eleventh Five Year
Plan on priority basis as thousands of
people may be benefited therefrom,
including unemployed youth, farmers and
tourists?
Financial assistance for Andhra
Pradesh projects
*319. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number and details of the
projects for which the State Government
of Andhra Pradesh has requested his
Ministry to provide financial assistance
under Externally Aided Projects (EAPs);
(b) the number of EAPs of the State for
which financial assistance has been released
by the Central Government alongwith those
for which financial assistance is still
awaited, indicating the amount released for
each of the sanctioned project; and
(c) by when Central financial assistance
is likely to be provided to the remaining
projects?

101
Share of shipping industries in goods
transportation
*320. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELW AL: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Shipping
industries’ share in transporting goods is
declining day by day in spite of growth of
import and export by 20 per cent;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that nearly
44 per cent of the existing vessels may be
retrieved by 2021; and
(d) the steps that have been taken or
proposed to be taken to improve the
condition of shipping industry?

Increase of power capacity by Atomic
Energy
†1785. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:

of indigenously produced uranium and
thorium, the generation of power can be
increased up to 30,000 MW in the coming
years in the country;

(c) whether it is also a fact that the
power generation capacity can be enhanced

nuclear technology

JOSHI:
SHRI RA VI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether any effort has been made
by Government to sign a bilateral
agreement to get civil nuclear technology
and related fuel from nuclear power
countries other than America;
(b) if so, the time by when this effort
was made and the countries involved
therein; and
(c) the reaction of the concerned
country after such efforts were made by
Government?

Setting up of nuclear power plant in
M.P.
†1787. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
of Madhya Pradesh has sent a proposal to
Central Government to install an Atomic
power plant in Madhya Pradesh;
(b) whether it is also a fact that he has
assured to install the plant by sanctioning
it expeditiously during his visit to Madhya
Pradesh; and
(c) if so, by when it would be
implemented and the present status of the
same?
Plan to boost research in nuclear sector
1788. DR. BARUN MUKHERJEE:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Department of Atomic
Energy (DAE) plans to boost research in
nuclear sector in the Eleventh Five Year
Plan;
(b) if so, the proposed budgetary
allocation and under what different heads,
in details; and
(c) whether this move indicates
Government's confidence in India's
capabilities to go ahead in nuclear energy
front without foreign assistance?
Self-reliance in the field of Atomic
Energy
1789. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARW AL: W ill the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a shortage of fuel
for atomic plants in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government is having any
plan to become self-reliant in the field of
atomic energy to ensure the atomic
autonomy; and
(d) if so, by when the country is likely
to become self-reliant in the field of atomic
fuel sector?
Coal blocks allocated for new power
plants
†1790. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the number of coal blocks allocated
in October, 2006-07 for setting up coal-
based new power plants in the private
sector;
(b) the volume of coal reserves in the
Chhattisgarh State in the country; and
(c) the time-frame within which power-
plants are to be set up by the companies
which had been allocated coal blocks in
Chhattisgarh and other State (Jharkhand)?

†1791. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that evidences of
99 billion tonnes of coal deposits have been
found in the country;
(b) if not, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that only
430 million tonnes of coal had been
produced in the year 2006-07 which was
less than the requirement of the country;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

(e) whether it is also a fact that the gap
between the demand and supply of coal at
the end of the Eleventh Plan is expected to

†1792. SHRI RAM

SHRI RA VI SHANKAR

Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased

(a) whether it is a fact that the coal wash
capacity in the country at present is only
15 per cent to 20 per cent of the total
production;
(b) if not, the details of this capacity in
March, 2007;

capacity is up to 80 per cent in coal export

change the present policy for leasing of
Lignite/Coal blocks;

deprive the rights of the State Government

priorities; and

peripheral villages

peripheral villages, their company-wise

amount was utilized; and

made about loss and profit as a result of
closure of these mines;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and

would deal with the problem of workers
going to be unemployed as a result of closure
of these mines?

(a) whether Government has taken a
decision to close some of the coal mines;

being closed; and

SULE:

communication policy

SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of

have made comprehensive changes in the
communication policy during the recent
past;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that
there is a resentment amongst the members
of Cellular Operators Association of India
due to the said changes;

the after effects of the said changes; and

SINGH MAJITHA:

the growth of big companies in the

difference between the growth rate of big

Madhubani, Bihar

COMMUNICATIONS AND

(a) whether it is a fact that Bharat
Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL), Bihar
Division is incurring losses to the tune of
lacs of rupees on account of telephone bills

number of members of the Telephone

surveillance

Will the Minister of

pleased to state:

the subscribers base of mobile telephone;
(b) if so, the details including the number
of subscribers for the last five years and
revenue from mobile services, year-wise,
State-wise and category-wise;
(c) if so, whether there is any scarcity

of COMMUNICATIONS AND

pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has made an
estimate with regard to the market value of
4.4 Mhz—6.2 Mhz GSM spectrum that

a price of Rs. 1651.57 crore; and
(b) if not, the basis on which this

COMMUNICATIONS AND

pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that under the
schemes such as speed post, delivery of
letters sent by ordinary mail from one city

Rameshwaram, Delhi to Chennai and Delhi

Jharkhand

Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the landline
phones of BSNL in rural areas of Jharkhand
are not functioning properly and repeated
complaints in this regard are being received;
(b) the details of the complaints received
during the last three years, year-wise;
(c) the main reason of these complaints;
and
(d) the average time taken to remove
these complaints?
Building for post offices in
Jharkhand
†1807. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of post offices being run
in rented buildings in Jharkhand and the
annual rent paid for these post offices;
(b) whether any scheme has been
prepared to provide permanent buildings
to these post offices; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS

be pleased to state:
(a) since when the practice of
publication of telephone directory was
started in telephone department in metro
cities and what was the purpose behind;
(b) reasons for stopping the publication
of the directory; and
(c) steps to be taken to restart this
publication?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

Routing of international calls
1809. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
